rows.description: A parent responds to distress with calm presence, names the feeling and repairs after their own mistakes. Perfection is not required; being reliably good enough is what builds trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, trust

rows.description: A child makes friends, handles quarrels and asks for help without shame. Assumes people generally mean well, and can recover after a disagreement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame

rows.subtype: Teen who stays connected while separating [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager argues, seeks independence and still comes home to talk when troubled. Attachment shows up as trust that the bond survives disagreement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust
possibly related concept (heuristic): Attachment-to-autonomy shifts

rows.description: A young adult can say what they need, tolerate a partner's need for space and repair after fights. Closeness and independence coexist without constant fear of loss.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, trust

rows.description: A friend notices someone who keeps promises, admits mistakes and does not make every disagreement a crisis. Such reliability is worth learning from, and is not the absence of hurt but the ability to repair.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: A partner feels steady when the other gives consistency, listens during conflict and does not punish honesty. Security makes it easier for both to be vulnerable and to grow.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: trust

rows.description: A toddler cries intensely when a caregiver leaves and is hard to settle on return, alternating between clinging and anger. Unsure comfort will be steady, so the child stays on alert.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger

rows.description: A child keeps checking where a parent is, asks repeatedly if they are loved and struggles with sleepovers. Fear of separation is real, and predictable goodbyes help more than dismissal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, fear

rows.description: A child fears being left out, over-reads a friend's silence and gets upset by any sign of preference for others. Needs help calming the alarm before deciding what the friend meant.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, anxiety, calm

rows.description: A parent or teacher sees a child who shadows adults and needs many reassurances. Rather than calling it attention-seeking, they offer steady warmth and small independence steps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
